-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”

Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 16, 2021

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Addleman, Bayer, Carman,  Carrese,
  Corman, Friedman, Medawar,  Schmitz,
  Seamans, Shinn, Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Arata, Buresh, Silvano

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Land Use Planner, Michael Baker International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES -
  JANUARY 19, 2021

B.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES -
  FEBRUARY 2, 2021

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BAYER to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEEETING MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 19. 2021 AND FEBRUARY 2, 2021.

There being not objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CITYWIDE LAND USE DISCUSSION

Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International, stated that there are a couple of sites that need
further discussion. The first site is at the southwest corner of Highridge Road and Armada Spring
Drive, which includes an office park of made up of five two-story buildings. The currently General
Plan Land Use (GPLU) is Commercial Office and the recommendation is to change this to
Neighborhood Commercial. This would make the site more compatible with the surrounding area,
which have a residential land use designation. In the future, there will be the flexibility to develop
this site as mixed-use.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE stated that these are individually owned “condos” used as
offices by residents of the surrounding area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN suggested that this should be changed to residential or
mixed-use.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if an owner changed from office to residential, how
would landscaping, setback and open space requirements be handled. Director Wahba stated
that this is a great point and could be an implementation measure discussed within zoning.
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE asked about the CC&R’s. Director Wahba stated that this
would be discussed with the property owners.

Ms. Barbhaya confirmed that there is consensus to change this site to Neighborhood Commercial.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that the next site to discuss is Academy Center, across from City Hall
(southwest corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Crenshaw Blvd.). The current GPLU is
Commercial Office and the recommendation is to expand it to allow for neighborhood commercial
uses. The current Commercial Office zoning will be amended to match the GPLU allowed Floor
Area Ratio FAR of 1.0 and allow Commercial Limited uses.

COMMITTEE ZUCKERMAN stated that this is a difficult intersection for people who are driving
east on Academy Drive and want to get into a left turning lane. The other exit on Crenshaw Blvd.
is also difficult due to those needing to make a left turn onto Crenshaw Blvd. Residential uses
generate fewer trips than office uses, but can still be an issue in the a.m. hours when people are
going to work or school

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that Crenshaw Blvd. is a County road and there are Senate Bills coming
out proposing legislation to boost housing; if more flexibility is given for residential, then there is
a concern with the proximity from PCH and Crenshaw Blvd. being a county road. CHAIR
SCHMITZ agrees with COMMITTEE ZUCKERMAN regarding traffic and density.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he understands zoning this residential will help
to meet the RHNA numbers but is concerned that now the site will be able to be developed by-
right without an EIR or an EIR that does not consider levels of service.

Mr. Bellas stated that on a 2.3 acre site and currently there are 40,000 sq. ft. of office space. On
a 2.3 acre site, the mixed-use overlay under the city’s designation would currently allow for 22-
units per acre and with the State density bonus of 50%, there would be an allowance for certain
affordable housing conceded by the developer. The total units at this site could be up to 75 units.
A trip generation projection could be, 1 trip per unit per day in the peak hour; 10 trips per unit per
day, which would be 75 trips in the morning hour or 10 trips every 6 minutes. Mr. Bellas stated
that office use would generate more trips in the peak hour.

In response to a question by Mr. Bellas, Director Wahba stated that for mixed-use developments
a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) and Precise Plan of Design (PPD) would be required. There
could be ways to consider Level of Service (LOS) under the CUP.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his concern with the city losing all discretion.

CHAIR SCHMITZ expressed her concern that in trying to be flexible, there is no consideration
with what the residents want or for what anyone locally deems appropriate.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER stated that the homeowner’s in Rollingwood are concerned with
the traffic impacts due to the developments in the Walteria area. There will be pushback from
homeowners and residents of the city for any development that will increase traffic flow and
population.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Barbhaya stated that
the RHNA numbers could be met through developments in the commercial district if there are
enough affordable housing options. The issue is that, even If the city mandates a certain
percentage of affordable housing and certain State bonuses, then you will still need more
affordable housing to meet the RHNA numbers. A plan would need to be produced to provide to
developers. The total RHNA number is 191.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested making the units 55+ since they would only be
allowed one parking spot and there is a bus stop nearby.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired about discussing a property on the outskirts of
the city that was discussed previously since it would not have as much traffic impact.

A discussion ensued on the suggestion to designate sites for 55+ residential units.

Mr. Bellas stated that there was discussion of two options: 1) To leave the sites as-is and is
enough land to meet the RHNA numbers elsewhere; if a developer decides to propose a mixed-
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
 use development, then it will need to go through the zone change amendment process. 2)
Develop a new GPLU designation for this site that allows for mixed use, but the residential
component is restricted to 55 and older independent living.

Mr. Bellas stated that as a CEQA practitioner, he would want the Land Use plan to be settled
before running the traffic model since one parcel makes a different. Also, the benefit of providing
direction through the General Plan for this site now would provide the property owner with
certainty on what the city envisions and would be supportive of for this property.

Planning Manager Naughton added that business operations are changing with commute type
remote working. Commercial Office designation is very limited in the uses that are allowed and
one of the concerns is to end up with a site that is underutilized and has high vacancies. Changing
this land use designation would allow for more flexibility for different use types.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER stated that she is not comfortable about limiting the site for 55
and older and thinks that this should be more flexible and can be anticipated as time went on. Ms.
Bayer also stated that there is an older demographic and this is a popular designation, but is
hesitant to limit other opportunities at this site.

COMMIITEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that this site for 55 and older makes sense but agreed
to be flexible.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that she is in favor of having the 55 and older
designation.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that currently Commercial Office does not allow for any retail use, so allowing
for neighborhood commercial uses would allow more flexibility. In addition, the recommendation
for this site is to extend the mixed-use overlay district to Commercial Office which will allow
residential development at this site.

There was consensus among the Committee Members to approve the recommendation as
presented.

B.  REFLECTIONS

Mr. Bellas provided an overview of the accomplishments of the General Plan Advisory Plan
Committee.

6.  FINAL COMMENTS AND NEXT STEPS

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the Michael Baker International Consultants for their professionalism,
incredible hard work, and keeping this project on schedule. She also expressed her gratitude to
the Committee for their passion and commitment to the City; from now to the next 40 years, your
voices will be heard.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his gratitude to CHAIR SCHMITZ for her work
and great work chairing this committee. He also thanked the Committee for their work.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if planning areas will be part of the General Plan
Update. Ms. Barbhaya stated that planning areas will not be part of the General Plan Update,
however, there will be a separate section for the Commercial District.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if there will be narrative about Neighborhood
Compatibility Determinations in the General Plan. Ms. Barbhaya stated that will be some language
on what kind of parameters need to be set for each of the land uses. In regards to the Commercial
District, one of the recommendations is to have a form based code. Director Wahba stated that in
regards to residential Neighborhood Compatibility, it is typically not included in the General Plan.
When a project is under planning review, the specific neighborhood is considered.

Ms. Barbhaya provided an overview of the upcoming meetings and next steps through plan
adoption.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN stated that it was an honor to be on this committee. She stated
that when looking back at the authors of the current General Plan, it is amazing to see how much

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING

 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
 they contributed since then and their guidance has given a good road map to maintain the
character of the community.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN stated that in response to COMMITTEE MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN’S comment regarding Neighborhood Compatibility, when projects are presented
to the Planning Commission, applicants think that there is subjectivitiy in decision making.
Anything that can be done to reinforce the character of the city in regards to scale, materials,
privacy is helpful in supporting decision making.

CITY MANAGER GRAMMER stated that he would like to recognize MAYOR ZUCKERMAN and
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ for their leadership and the excellent work that they have done in
chairing these meetings for three plus years. He also thanked the Michael Baker International
Consultants for their expertise and guidance. He also thanked staff and most importantly thanked
the Committee for their time and dedication to this important process and this has been critical in
guiding the future of the City. It is your community and we want to make sure the quality of life
that you enjoy continues for generations to come.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 7:15 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

____________________________________  _____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
